decision.reason: Prior adjudication files do not yet exist; the old Chan Wing Yan cache and collection timecap are unrelated history. In the verified 98-page Chan On Ying (2021) thesis (osf.io/u59ab), page 6 explicitly identifies Young & Saxe (2011), 'When ignorance is no excuse: Different roles for intent across moral domains', Cognition, 120(2), 202-214, DOI 10.1016/j.cognition.2011.04.005, as the sole target research article, re-testing Experiments 1A and 2 to 4 in a combined mixed-design experiment (pp. 7, 11-15, 17-18). Other cited works—including Sweetman & Newman (2020) on Experiment 1B (p. 10) and Parkinson & Byrne (2016/2018) on moral responsibility (pp. 11, 16-17, 45)—serve as background or extension motivation rather than re-tested targets, and the cached 2egqr Stage 1 draft is not used as evidence.

decision.reason: The Abstract (p. 7) explicitly states an overall set-wide verdict: 'we successfully replicated and extended Experiments 1A, and 2 to 4 from Young and Saxe (2011)', reinforced by the formal LeBel et al. evaluation (Table 5, p. 21; p. 41) and Discussion opening ('We successfully replicated all of the original significant effects... Overall, with a larger well-powered sample, this replication echoes with the original study', p. 42). Under Codebook Step 3 Rule 1 and the mixed-category rule ('only an overall verdict that speaks to the replication as a whole (rule 1) outweighs a stated contrast'), this explicit whole-target verdict governs over the partial support on reframed Hypotheses 2 and 3 (pp. 37-38) and the Discussion/Conclusion contrasts (pp. 42-45, 47) noting that patterns (1) and (2) were not specific to moral wrongness versus disgust and emotion ratings. Supplementary pages 93-95 document correcting a Qualtrics scale-coding typo (Int_harm_ER) before data collection and recoding the Jamovi template variable for accuracy, not a methodological flaw or uninformative verdict.

Power analysis and Participants

       We calculated the overall required sample size (0.95 power and 0.05 alpha) as 423, based on

the lowest effect size of the combined experiments from Experiment 3, see Table 5 for overall effects

and power analyses, and supplementary for more details. We aimed for a high power given allocated

budget, so following Simonsohn (2015) general rule of thumb of 2.5 we aimed for 1000 participants.


       A total of 1006 American Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk) participants completed the

study using TurkPrime.com (Mage = 42.0, SD = 12.9; 493 females). We provided a comparison of the

target article samples and the replication samples in Table 4. We summarised
decision.reason: The study collected new empirical data from an online sample of American Amazon Mechanical Turk participants (N = 1006 analyzed, N = 1009 in Table 4; pp. 7, 19-20, 29-41) to re-test and extend Experiments 1A and 2 to 4 from Young & Saxe (2011). Supplementary effect-size and power calculations computed from the original paper's published summary statistics (pp. 68-81) and pre-/post-exclusion analyses of the new replication sample (pp. 72-73, 91-92) do not re-analyse original participant data. Under Codebook Step 1, collecting new data in a new sample to re-test published findings is a replication.
